name: Solenne Pavilion
description:
Solenne Pavilion occupies the 87th through 91st floors of the Meridian Solenne Tower in the Spire's cultural district, a purpose-built concert complex completed in 2215 at a construction cost of approximately Φ4.2 billion. The main hall seats 1,800 in neural-sync chairs — each seat individually calibrated to the occupant's BCI profile, allowing the performance to be experienced simultaneously as sound, tactile sensation, and directed emotional modulation at the listener's chosen intensity. The acoustic design uses active cancellation and directional amplification to create a listening environment that critics have described as 'the inside of the music rather than the outside.' The building's exterior is a continuous curved glass surface that functions as a passive holographic projector, visible from much of the upper city.

Solenne Pavilion is operated by Aurantia Cultural Holdings, a Tier 5 investment consortium, and tickets for premium neural-sync seating begin at Φ2,400. A separate standing gallery accessible from a different entrance offers reduced-neural or audio-only experiences at Φ180–400, technically making the venue accessible to Tier 3 audiences, though the social and spatial design of the building ensures these audiences rarely interact. The Pavilion hosts the annual Meridian Composition Prize ceremony and serves as the primary venue for visiting ensembles from other megacity corridors. Notable events include the 2219 world premiere of 'Spire Sequence No. 13,' which caused three audience members to experience extended dissociative states from the neural-sync intensity, resulting in a temporary regulatory review of the hall's BCI broadcast parameters.
creator: Aurantia Cultural Holdings, commissioned 2212, opened 2215
genre: Orchestral, neural composition, holographic ensemble, commissioned contemporary work
audience: Tier 5 cultural elite, Tier 4 corporate entertainment accounts, Tier 3 aspirational attendees in the gallery, visiting dignitaries, international music press
cultural_impact: Solenne Pavilion represents the apex of GLMZ's official cultural infrastructure and the full expression of what wealth can do to music — transforming it from communication into luxury product. Its neural-sync technology has genuinely advanced the art form, and several compositions premiered here have entered the broader cultural conversation across tiers. At the same time, the venue functions as a social sorting mechanism, its price structure and spatial design ensuring that the experience of Solenne is understood as a marker of class position as much as aesthetic engagement. the Gray Zone and Circuit musicians speak of it with a mixture of contempt and covetous fascination.
known_fans: Tier 5 corporate executives and their families
composers seeking the Meridian Composition Prize
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone musician receives a commission to perform at Solenne Pavilion — the first Tier 1 resident to do so — and the terms of the contract include a clause that would transfer creative ownership of all works performed to Aurantia Cultural Holdings in perpetuity. They have 72 hours to decide.

The dissociative states during the 2219 premiere were not a calibration error. Someone embedded a rogue neural sequence in the performance score, and the regulatory review buried the finding. It's happening again at the next premiere.

A Tier 4 attendee in the standing gallery experiences something during a performance that they cannot explain — a memory that isn't theirs, vivid and complete. They begin to investigate whether the neural-sync system can be used to transfer more than sensation.
